owned_invariants: Each entry hash is SHA-256 of the domain line and the JSON of (seq, prev, record); replay refuses any edit, reorder or gap as CHAIN_BROKEN.
A failure is typed by the canon (failure class, DDC letters) and binds a 64-hex evidence hash.
A candidate rule must cite recorded failures; its trial must be on held-out failures disjoint from those.
A rule is admitted only while it is a candidate whose latest trial beat the baseline with zero hits on clean work; retirement is final.
admitted() lists exactly the rules a later run may load.
boundaries: The ledger records what a host reports; it does not run the trial itself.
Counts are compared, not combined, so there is no arithmetic to overflow.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed vocabularies from the canon, checked arithmetic, no unwrap or direct indexing.

basis.G1: Module header declares AuthorityEffect None and the contract URN; public items match this contract and code/rust/pfp_operads/README.md. Not B: no requirement-to-symbol trace beyond the README and docs/plans/operads_redesign.md.
basis.G2: Non-numeric: counts are compared only. Statuses and vocabularies come from the canon. The hash input is the serde_json encoding of a fixed tuple, checked by a by-hand hash test.
basis.G3: Thirteen typed refusal codes; a refused record leaves the ledger unchanged; unknown fields are denied on replay. Not B: panic-freedom is tested, not proven.
basis.G4: 11 ledger tests cover the admission lifecycle, each refusal, replay, tamper detection and the by-hand hash. One mutant is recorded as demonstrably equivalent with its justification in the report. clippy -D warnings and rustfmt pass. Lexical mutation campaign R = 25/25. Not B: mutants are hand-written one-line edits, not a generated campaign, and there are no generator-driven property tests.
basis.G5: lizard: worst cyclomatic 4, nesting 4; ceiling B. Cognitive complexity is not measured for Rust; complexipy was stubbed for the metrics run because it only reads .py files.

report.note: lexical campaign, 26 one-line mutants, crate tests as oracle
